Cell round 3b: animation-ready, and four wardrobes

Brief 012 round 3b · Forma · 2026-10-15 · Codex only (no Qwen this round; ceiling total $1.809 of $3.00 after round 3). Faces, bodies, hair from the A portraits; signature items and silhouette shapes kept; animation rules kept (hems at hip or mid-thigh, no capes, structured trousers flagged). Thumbnails embedded; click for full files; model, prompt, refs, sha256 in PROVENANCE.json.

Answer to Sky: is each character dressed very differently?

L1 was not: four silhouettes and four signature items, but one palette, one material language and one fashion lineage, a squad uniform. Round 3b stage 1 (white on charcoal, hip-length) fixed the animation problem only. Stage 2 gives each person their own palette, materials and fashion lineage and ties the team together with one small motif. Compare the three rows in section 3.

1. Four wardrobes

Each person has a dominant colour plus one accent, their own materials, and a fashion lineage from a different subculture of their home timeline. Rules held: hems at the hip or mid-thigh at most, no capes or tails, structured trousers only (flagged), ponytail as one secondary chain.

Animation notes (estimates from the drawings; no rig built)

Base rig: the 65-bone Mixamo humanoid of the pipeline. 'Extra bones' are over those 65. Cloth-sim risk is whether the garment needs sim or heavy corrective skinning; the set is built so none needs a cloth sim. One lineup adds about 16 to 18 bones over 4 x 65, roughly 7 percent.

2. Palettes and the signals

Gate: dE2000 20 or more from cone red #e03a2f, guard amber #f0a020, rival violet #8a4fd0 (unlit). Also checked against the city's own palette (cream, peach, mint, seafoam, deep teal, turquoise, cobalt, flamingo, sunshine, asphalt, park, lagoon): none of the four is cream or seafoam. The search space is narrow: of 31 candidate colours only 17 clear both the signals and the city; the best four-set is separated by dE 23 at most.

As painted, at 50 px

Per figure: the largest colour clusters of the painting after removing skin and near-black outlines (crude), then the average dE between two figures' cluster sets (each cluster to the nearest in the other, weighted). Larger = the figures differ more in colour.

WB1-pin: Wardrobes + Visitor's pin6.710.7four palettes
WB2-chevron: Wardrobes + chrome chevron8.110.5four palettes
WB3-lamp: Wardrobes + lamp bead7.49.7four palettes

The wardrobes are about three times further apart in colour than the uniform rows, but the absolute figures (about 7 to 13) are modest: the painted garments render darker and duller than their target hexes (matte leather, canvas and knit in soft light). To read apart at 50 px by colour alone, lift the base values (khaki, moss and chestnut each about 10 L higher) or give the accents bigger areas. The 50 px views in section 4 already read as four different people.

3. Team thread and lineups

Three motifs proposed, one per lineup, same four people each time: M1 Visitor's pin (a chrome ring-with-a-bar pin, worn on the pack strap, collar, visor edge, shoulder), M2 Chrome chevron (a small chrome chevron badge on the left upper arm or shoulder, in each person's own material), M3 Lamp bead (a small chrome-rimmed bead that glows pale aqua, on the earpiece, case latch, visor, rifle; it lights when that person acts). All three read in portraits and close-ups; at 50 px none survives as paint (see the x5 thumbnails). M3 is the only one that can survive at 50 px as an emissive sprite with bloom, and it carries a gameplay meaning (who is acting), so it is my pick; its pale aqua is dE 10 from the city's mint, so keep it small and glowing, not a surface. M1 is the fallback for HUD portraits.

The comparison: L1 uniform / animatable uniform / four wardrobes

4. Silhouette test at 50 px

Black fills of the five lineups, and the whole lineup at play scale: tallest figure 56 px after the 38 degree camera's foreshortening (height x cos 38), shown at native size and at 5x. Profile distance = how different the width-over-height outlines are (higher = more distinct; the closest pair matters). IoU = true-scale silhouette overlap (lower = more distinct). Figures: 0 Scout, 1 Fixer, 2 Tech, 3 Enforcer.

The 50 px view shows the real gain: the wardrobes read as four different people by colour and the yoke and shoulder-rifle poses make nameable shadows; the uniform rows read as one squad. 5. Cosplay sheets (top take per person)

Front and back turnaround and three numbered callouts each. Back views are the model's invention from the front: check before building. Scout, Fixer, Tech and Enforcer tops are the trail runner, knit tunic, canvas apron and lacquer yoke (the Enforcer's across-the-shoulders pose Sky liked).

6. Stage 1: the L1 look made animatable (white on charcoal), superseded by section 1

Twelve takes plus the carried-over Scout. All meet the hem rules; kept for the comparison row and because they are the cheapest rig variants.

7. Iteration log

Palette A wardrobes (graphite, navy, olive, cocoa: too dark, too close), a first set of lineups that Codex drew as portrait pictures with feet cropped (fixed by checking the aspect and retrying), and palette A cosplay sheets.
